assumptions: Each variable's mean and SD (or its replicates) describe its uncertainty; covariances are used only when asked.
limits: The Taylor arm is exact only for a linear expression; a ratio is not linear, so compare it with the simulation.
Systematic error (a wrong efficiency, a biased calibrator) is not in the spread.
bio.jane/contract.question: How uncertain is a reported qPCR quantity, given the uncertainty of each measurement in it, and which measurement contributes most?

description: Uncertainty through any qPCR quantity, three independent ways at once. Give it the expression you actually report - a ratio, a normalised expression, an efficiency-corrected quantity - and a mean and standard deviation for each variable in it (or the replicate observations themselves), and it returns the analytic Taylor propagation, a Monte-Carlo simulation and a permutation resampling side by side, because they disagree in informative ways: the Taylor arm is exact only for a linear expression, and a ratio is not linear. Also reports the derivative per variable and how much of the total variance each one contributes, which is the answer to "which measurement should I make more precisely?". Reproduces qpcR 1.4.2's `propagate`.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

conf_level.description: the level the reported bounds are read at.

dist_sim.description: the distribution drawn from: `norm`, or `tnorm` truncated at zero — the one to use when a variable is a concentration or a fluorescence and a negative draw is not a possible measurement. Only applies when do_sim is true.

do_perm.description: `raw` only: run the permutation arm, which resamples the observed rows and so assumes no distribution at all. It also returns p-values for the three hypotheses upstream tests. Only applies when input is raw.

do_sim.description: run the Monte-Carlo arm — draw from the joint normal and push every draw through the expression. Correct for any nonlinearity, at the cost of being a sample.

expression.description: the quantity whose uncertainty is wanted, in R's syntax over the variable names below: `x/y`, `2^-(a - b)`, `(Etar^-Cttar)/(Eref^-Ctref)`. Every name in it must appear in `variables`.

input.description: what `variables` holds. `stat` = a summary per variable; `raw` = the replicate observations. `raw` is the stronger input: it carries the measured covariance between variables and it is the only one the permutation arm can resample, because permutation resamples observed ROWS and a mean with an SD beside it has none.

nperm.description: permutations. Only applies when do_perm is true.

nsim.description: Monte-Carlo draws. Only applies when do_sim is true.

second_order.description: include the second-order Taylor terms. On is upstream's default and is what makes the analytic arm usable on a ratio; off gives the classic first-order propagation of error.

seed.description: R's `set.seed` value, so a simulated or permuted run is reproducible and citable. Advanced.

ties.description: `raw` only: which columns are resampled together, as one whole number per column — `1,1,2` permutes the first two as a block. Blank permutes every column on its own. Use it when two columns are readings of the same tube. Only applies when do_perm is true.

use_cov.description: `raw` only: propagate the measured covariance between the variables, not just their variances. Two Ct values read off the same plate are not independent, and treating them as independent understates the error of their ratio. Only applies when input is raw.

variables.description: the numbers. In `stat` mode: a header row `variable, mean, sd` and one row per variable. In `raw` mode: a header row of variable names and one row per replicate, blank cells left blank (they are dropped pairwise, never read as zero). Tab- or comma-separated.

name: propagate_uncertainty

contributions.description: how much of the propagated variance each variable contributes, in %, first-order — which measurement to make more precisely

firstOrderMean.description: the expression evaluated at the input means, before the second-order correction

gradient.description: the printed partial derivative per variable, and its value at the means

permPValues.description: permutation p-values for the three hypotheses upstream tests, in `perm > init` / `perm == init` / `perm < init` order

permuted.description: the permutation arm, same fields. Null in `stat` mode, which has no rows to resample

propagatedMean.description: the expression evaluated at the input means, with the second-order correction when it is on

propagatedSd.description: the analytic (Taylor) standard error — the number to report when the expression is close to linear

secondOrderMean.description: the mean with the second-order Taylor correction applied, whether or not the reported mean uses it

simulated.description: the Monte-Carlo arm: mean, sd, median, mad and its own interval. Every field null when it was not run — a nonlinear expression whose two arms disagree is the finding, not a display detail

variables.description: the variable names the run used, in expression order — every other array here is in this order
